comparison: Both address Hox upregulation claims (C2, C36-C41). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED based on multiple methods (microarray, RNA-seq, qRT-PCR), while peer review rates it UNCERTAIN due to inability to detect Hox upregulation by in situ hybridization, considering this a major weakness despite qPCR data.

Both evaluate snRNA-seq analysis (C3, C42-C46, C50-C52, C112). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes robust cell numbers and distinct Hox patterns, while peer review accepts the data as solid evidence without specific challenges.

Both address disrupted Hox pattern in PN regions (C4, C61, C115). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on qRT-PCR data, while peer review rates UNCERTAIN due to concerns about interpretation in context of previous work and lack of in situ validation.

Both evaluate cortex-PN connectivity defects (C5, C64, C65, C102, C116). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes lack of functional assessment and causal link to Hox dysregulation. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, emphasizing the tenuous link between molecular findings and circuit phenotype, and lack of rescue experiments for axon targeting.

Both address RNF220-WDR5 interaction and regulation (C7, C74-C79, C103). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with comprehensive biochemical evidence. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, with reviewer stating in vitro data is convincing. Peer review includes additional ubiquitination claims (C80-C91) that OpenEval addresses separately in R7.

Both evaluate region-specific WDR5 accumulation (C69-C73). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes spatial specificity correlating with Hox upregulation, while peer review accepts the data without specific challenges.

OpenEval R7 addresses comprehensive ubiquitination analysis (C81-C91) and rates SUPPORTED. Peer review R5 includes these claims along with interaction data and also rates SUPPORTED, stating the in vitro biochemical data is convincing.

Both evaluate P19 cell system demonstrating Rnf220-Wdr5-Hox regulatory relationship (C10, C11, C48, C92, C111). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes partial rescue suggesting additional mechanisms, while peer review finds the in vitro data convincing.

Both address WDR5 inhibitor rescue (C8, C94). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes lack of information on injection efficiency and long-term effects. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, emphasizing lack of validation by methods other than qRT-PCR and lack of functional rescue of circuit phenotype.

Both evaluate genetic rescue with conditional Wdr5 deletion (C9, C98). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes limited sample size and lack of circuit rescue data. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, noting rescue shown only in vitro and lack of in vivo validation beyond qPCR or functional circuit analysis.

Both address epigenetic changes at Hox loci in vivo (C66, C67). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes limited analysis and lack of direct WDR5 binding demonstration. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, noting incomplete epigenetic data (not all Hox5 paralogs) and tenuous links to phenotype.

Both evaluate epigenetic changes in P19 cells (C99, C100). OpenEval includes these in broader epigenetic analysis (R11) rated SUPPORTED. Peer review R11 specifically addresses P19 ChIP-qPCR data and rates SUPPORTED, with no specific challenges to in vitro epigenetic data.
OpenEval R12 addresses PN morphology analysis (C62, C63) and rates SUPPORTED, noting no structural differences despite molecular changes. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval R13 addresses PN marker upregulation (C53, C57) and rates SUPPORTED but notes unclear biological significance. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval R14 addresses lack of PcG component changes (C68) and rates SUPPORTED, supporting specificity of WDR5 regulation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval R15 addresses RA-dependency of RNF220-WDR5-Hox axis (C49, C93, C120) and rates SUPPORTED but notes lack of mechanistic explanation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R16 addresses region-specific WDR5 regulation despite widespread RNF220 expression (C108, C117, C118) and rates SUPPORTED, noting context-dependent regulation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval R17 addresses WDR5 truncation analysis localizing ubiquitination sites (C87) and rates SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R18 addresses glycinergic neuron identity and Hox7-10 expression (C113) and rates UNCERTAIN, noting need for careful examination of expression claims. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R19 addresses speculative claims about Hox dysregulation causing circuit defects (C109, C114) and rates UNCERTAIN, noting lack of causal testing. This concern overlaps with peer review R4's concerns about tenuous links, but no direct peer evaluation of these specific claims.

OpenEval R20 addresses speculative interpretation of RA-dependency mechanism (C122) and rates UNCERTAIN, noting this is hypothesis rather than demonstrated result. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
